_provenance.what: The official AAMC MCAT content outline: 4 sections, 10 foundational concepts, 31 content categories (9 bio/biochem + 10 chem/phys + 12 psych/soc). This is the denominator for the PRD §8 coverage map - 'every topic on the official outline, marked covered or not'.
_provenance.how_this_was_built: Content category codes and titles were transcribed from a third-party compilation (https://medlifemastery.com/mcat/content-review/aamc-outline/) and then spot-verified directly against AAMC's own pages. Verified verbatim against AAMC: Foundational Concept 1's statement and categories 1A/1B/1C/1D (https://students-residents.aamc.org/biological-and-biochemical-foundations-living-systems/biological-and-biochemical-foundations-living-systems-foundational-concept-1), category 4A (https://students-residents.aamc.org/chemical-and-physical-foundations-biological-systems-foundational-concept-4/chemical-and-physical-foundations-biological-systems-section-content-category-4a), and category 10A (https://students-residents.aamc.org/applying-medical-school/article/mcat-2015-content-category-10a/). The remaining categories match that same compilation, which agreed exactly with AAMC on every spot-check; they were NOT each individually re-verified against AAMC. Stated plainly rather than implied: this file is a faithful transcription with partial direct verification, not a scrape of the official PDF.
_provenance.foundational_concept_statements: Only FC1's statement is reproduced verbatim from AAMC (it was the one fetched directly). The others are omitted rather than paraphrased from memory - an outline is a factual document and inventing its wording would be exactly the kind of thing this project's honesty rule forbids.
_provenance.topic_tag_mapping: The `topic_tags` arrays are OURS, not AAMC's. They map this collection's `topic::<name>` tags onto content categories. Categories with tags have real curriculum source material behind them in speedrun/ai/ (see sources.json) and cards generated from it - a tag is only added here once genuine source content exists for that category, never to make the coverage number look better. Categories with no tags have no material yet; that is the honest state and is precisely what the coverage map is supposed to expose.
_provenance.dok_profile: Typical Depth-of-Knowledge range per MCAT section, used by the v3 give-up rule to decide which topics the latency-volatility (rote-pattern) check should be applied to. PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY: these ranges are NOT published by AAMC. They were derived from user-supplied research on Socratic-method effectiveness by section, which classified sections by the depth of reasoning their items demand. That research's strongest specific figure (r = 0.457) traced to an undergraduate senior thesis, n = 34, p > 0.01, and correlational; its remaining claims arrived as bracketed citations without resolvable sources and were never independently verified. The DOK ranges are therefore a defensible editorial judgement about exam structure, not a sourced fact, and should be treated as tunable configuration rather than ground truth. The original per-section Socratic bridge policy that shipped alongside these ranges was removed with the v2 tutor (see speedrun/docs/pivot-plan-latency-volatility.md Phase 1); only the DOK ranges survived, because v3 needs to know which content is reasoning-heavy. LIMITATION, UNCHANGED: DOK is really a property of a card, not a section - amino acid structures are DOK 1 rote even though bio/biochem is a reasoning-heavy section. Per-card DOK labelling is not built, so a `dok::N` note tag overrides the section default where it matters.

sections.name: Biological and Biochemical Foundations of Living Systems

foundational_concepts.statement: Biomolecules have unique properties that determine how they contribute to the structure and function of cells, and how they participate in the processes necessary to maintain life.

content_categories.title: Structure and function of proteins and their constituent amino acids
Transmission of genetic information from the gene to the protein
Transmission of heritable information from generation to generation and the processes that increase genetic diversity
Principles of bioenergetics and fuel molecule metabolism
Assemblies of molecules, cells, and groups of cells within single cellular and multicellular organisms
The structure, growth, physiology, and genetics of prokaryotes and viruses
Processes of cell division, differentiation, and specialization
Structure and functions of the nervous and endocrine systems and ways in which these systems coordinate the organ systems
Structure and integrative functions of the main organ systems

dok_profile.rationale: Systems and mechanisms: questions ask you to reason along a pathway, so retrieval is usually reconstruction rather than lookup.

dok_profile.rationale: Quantitative relationships: questions ask what happens to Y when X changes, so retrieval usually involves a derivation step.

sections.name: Critical Analysis and Reasoning Skills
sections.no_outline_reason: CARS has no memorizable content outline - it is a pure reasoning section over passages drawn from humanities and social sciences. A flashcard deck structurally cannot 'cover' it, so it is excluded from the coverage denominator rather than counted as permanently 0% (which would understate coverage in a misleading way). This is a real limitation of a flashcard-based readiness model, not a gap to be papered over: a student at 100% content coverage still has an unmeasured quarter of the exam.

dok_profile.rationale: No memorisable content at all; every item is reasoning over an unseen passage.
